newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end lower with further losses seen.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end lower with further losses seen.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed lower in rangebound trade, as players squared positions before the first notice day for the July contract, dealers said.
While the spot July contract managed to hold above its recent low of 71.30 cents, market sources said the overall trend remains lower, and pegged firm support at 70.00 cents.
"Supplies will continue to weigh on the market," a trader said.
In addition to an ongoing bearish fundamental situation, the NYCE noted that open interest in the FCOJ futures market stood at a record 36,791 lots as of the close Monday.
The increase in liquidity comes amid declining prices, suggesting that further losses may be in store.
The spec/hedge report released today noted a 26 percent net speculative short position as of June 20, up from 21 percent the previous week, NYCE said today.

The spot July contract settled 0.65 cent lower at 73.65 cents per lb, traded 74.40 to 73.60 cents. The most-active September contract ended down 0.70 cent at 76.50 cents, while the rest of the board finished 0.55 to 0.35 cent weaker.
Activity will focus on the liquidation of the spot month ahead of first notice day on July 1. Open interest in July stood at 10,820 lots, down 1,596 lots, as of Tuesday.
An estimated 7,000 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Tuesday's official 5,516 lots.
